text:
lina: Quick question 1 planning to be in Seoul Apr 15  Aug 10 (about 4 months). Do I need to do anything for benefits, visa, payroll? Also curious if WFH stipend continues and whether we can ship a monitor.
people-ops: Hey @lina  thanks for flagging. High-level: submit the Homebase Change form (https://redwood.company/forms/homebase), note travel dates, and select temporary residency. We'll run checks for payroll, benefits coverage, and any local regs. Stipend usually continues and is prorated for partial months.
hr-benefits: Hi @lina  two quick notes: 1) US group medical typically doesn't extend coverage overseas except in emergencies. We recommend buying short-term international medical or using our global medical rider (if eligible). 2) Retirement/pension: you remain on US 401(k) contributions while on payroll, but if local social security applies we may need to pause or register. We'll confirm after payroll/tax check.
tax-eng: @lina heads-up: Korea uses a substantial presence test and has an income tax system + social security rules. Under many circumstances <183 days means no permanent establishment for the company, but other factors (e.g., client meetings, recruiting, signing contracts) can create nexus. Please confirm if you'll meet local customers or attend conferences while there. We'll run a quick nexus review once homebase form is in.
lina: No client meetings planned, purely dev & async. Might attend a local meetup but not representing Redwood.
it-ship: If you need a monitor shipped, we have a temporary shipping cap of $1,500 for short-term remote requests (different from relocation cap). Please open a ticket with `#it-ship` and include asset tag + delivery address in Seoul. We require receipts for customs clearance.
people-ops: Also FYI on payroll: unless we route you through an EOR for Korea you'll stay on USD payroll. That can create withholding nuances; we'll confirm with payroll ops. Stipend proration example: ``prorated = monthly_amount * (days_in_country / days_in_month)``.
people-ops-bot: Policy update: "Temporary Remote: Asia short trips" added to policy hub: https://redwood.company/policies/temporary-remote-asia. Checklist attached in doc (passport, visa copy if applicable, local contact, receipts).
hr-benefits: Action for @lina: 1) upload copy of passport + flight, 2) indicate whether you'll enroll in company global rider or buy private travel medical, 3) confirm monitor request in `#it-ship`. We'll coordinate any 401(k) changes if payroll routing changes.
people-ops: We'll queue the tax nexus review  expect update in 2 business days after form submission. If nexus risk is flagged we'll reach out about potential EOR routing.
lina: Thanks y'all. Submitted form and uploaded flight. Requested monitor in `#it-ship` (monitor-asset-449). Cheers :sparkles:
